questions.prompt: The mountains had echoed with the shouts of the victors.
questions.answer: Montēs clāmōribus victōrum resonāverant.

questions.prompt: When the messenger has announced the news, the city will rejoice.
questions.answer: Ubi nūntius rem nūntiāverit, urbs gaudēbit.

questions.prompt: If we have defended the walls bravely, the fatherland will be safe.
questions.answer: Sī mūrōs fortiter dēfenderimus, patria salva erit.

questions.prompt: The pale merchant had lost all his money in the shipwreck.
questions.answer: Mercātor pallidus omnem pecūniam naufragiō āmīserat.

questions.prompt: When you have cut off the branches, carry them into the house.
questions.answer: Ubi rāmōs abscīderis, eōs in domum portā.

questions.prompt: The god had permitted mortals to gaze upon the stars.
questions.answer: Deus mortālibus sīdera vidēre permīserat.

questions.prompt: After the storm had subsided, the fishermen sought the tranquil shore.
questions.answer: Postquam procella cōnsēderat, piscātōrēs lītus tranquillum petīvērunt.

questions.prompt: The old man had cut down the tall tree with a heavy axe.
questions.answer: Senex arborem altam gravī secūrī abscīderat.

questions.prompt: The victors had appeased the angry gods with many sacrifices.
questions.answer: Victōrēs deōs īrātōs multīs sacrificiīs plācāverant.

questions.prompt: When you have read the letter, you will understand the whole plan.
questions.answer: Cum epistulam lēgeris, tōtum cōnsilium intellegēs.

questions.prompt: If the king will have conquered the enemy, the citizens will rejoice.
questions.answer: Sī rēx hostēs vīcerit, cīvēs gaudēbunt.

questions.prompt: As soon as the messenger will have arrived, we will announce the victory.
questions.answer: Simulac nūntius advēnerit, victōriam nūntiābimus.

questions.prompt: The Cyclops, once the sheep had been devoured, had fallen into a deep sleep.
questions.answer: Cyclōps, ovibus dēvorātīs, in altum somnum ceciderat.

questions.prompt: The rough road had broken the wheels of the chariot.
questions.answer: Via aspera rotās currūs frēgerat.

questions.prompt: The general had drawn up the battle line before dawn.
questions.answer: Dux aciem ante lūcem īnstrūxerat.

questions.prompt: The wretched captives had endured many hardships in chains.
questions.answer: Captīvī miserrimī multōs labōrēs in catēnīs tolerāverant.

questions.prompt: If you will have hidden the treasure well, no thief will find it.
questions.answer: Sī thēsaurum bene cēlāveris, nūllus fūr eum inveniet.

questions.prompt: After the enemies have fled, the fields will grow green again.
questions.answer: Postquam hostēs fūgerint, agrī iterum virēscent.

questions.prompt: You will have earned great praise when you have served the state faithfully.
questions.answer: Magnam laudem merueris cum reī pūblicae fidēliter dēservieris.

questions.prompt: The frightened horse had thrown the rider onto the hard ground.
questions.answer: Equus territus equitem in dūram humum dēiēcerat.

questions.prompt: The poet had sung of the wanderings of brave Ulysses.
questions.answer: Poēta errōrēs fortis Ulixis cecinerat.

questions.prompt: Before the trumpet sounded, the soldiers had abandoned the camp.
questions.answer: Antequam tuba sonuit, mīlitēs castra relīquerant.

questions.prompt: The savage tempest had scattered the ships across the whole sea.
questions.answer: Saeva tempestās nāvēs per tōtum mare disiēcerat.

questions.prompt: When the sun has set, the shepherds will have led the goats home.
questions.answer: Cum sōl occiderit, pāstōrēs capellās domum dūxerint.

questions.prompt: By nightfall you will have crossed the broad river with the army.
questions.answer: Sub noctem flūmen lātum cum exercitū trānsieris.

questions.prompt: The maiden had concealed her tears from her stern father.
questions.answer: Virgō lacrimās ā sevērō patre abdiderat.

questions.prompt: As soon as I have finished the work, I will seek quiet rest.
questions.answer: Simulac opus perfēcerō, quiētam requiem petam.

questions.prompt: When I have written the letter, I will send a swift messenger.
questions.answer: Cum epistulam scrīpserō, nūntium celerem mittam.

questions.prompt: If you will have seen a tiger in the forest, you will flee at once.
questions.answer: Sī tigrim in silvā vīderis, statim fugiēs.

questions.prompt: When we have prepared the dinner, we will call our friends to the table.
questions.answer: Ubi cēnam parāverimus, amīcōs ad mēnsam vocābimus.

questions.prompt: After the executioner has departed, the joyful citizens will return home.
questions.answer: Postquam carnifex abierit, cīvēs laetī domum redībunt.

questions.prompt: The son, who had lost all the money, had exasperated his father.
questions.answer: Fīlius, quī omnem pecūniam perdiderat, patrem exasperāverat.

questions.prompt: The clever merchant had imported much timber from Egypt.
questions.answer: Mercātor callidus multam materiam ex Aegyptō importāverat.

questions.prompt: The maidservant had placed flowers and oregano in the inner garden.
questions.answer: Ancilla flōrēs et orīganum in hortō intimō posuerat.

questions.prompt: If you burn the letter, no one will know our plan.
questions.answer: Sī epistulam cremāveris, nēmō cōnsilium nostrum sciet.

questions.prompt: When the tiger has escaped from the cage, all the spectators will be terrified.
questions.answer: Ubi tigris ē caveā effūgerit, omnēs spectātōrēs pavēbunt.

questions.prompt: When we have heard the teacher, we will be better students.
questions.answer: Cum magistrum audīverimus, meliōrēs discipulī erimus.

questions.prompt: After the soldiers have captured the city, they will lead the queen away as a captive.
questions.answer: Postquam mīlitēs urbem cēperint, rēgīnam captīvam dūcent.
